title: Accessing and Navigating the Deception Admin Portal

blocks.text: This article covers the following topics:

blocks.item: Signing In to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal
After your organization is provisioned for Zscaler Deception, you will receive an email with the following details:
Link to your Deception instance
Link to set your password
Security code
To sign in to the Deception Admin Portal:
Click the password link in your email.
On the Reset Password page, enter a new password and confirm it.
Enter the Security Code from your email.
See image.
Click Next.
Scan the QR code that appears using a two-factor authentication (2FA) app to complete the 2FA configuration.
See image.
Enter the One-Time Password (OTP), which is a 6-digit code shown on the authenticator app.
Click Submit.
When the Sign In page appears, enter your Email and Password.
See image.
Click Sign in.
When the Two-factor authentication page appears, enter the 2FA code from the authenticator app.
See image.
Click Submit.
If you're subscribed to Authentication Service:
Log in to the Authentication Service landing page.
Based on your organization's authentication preference, sign in to Authentication Service using one of the following methods:
Password
Email One-Time Password (OTP)
Security Key or Biometric
Enter your login ID. If you want the service to remember your login ID the next time you log in, select the Remember Me checkbox.
See image.
Click Next.
Enter your password and click Sign In.
See image.
Based on your organization's MFA policy, 2FA is required. Complete your 2FA to access the Authentication Service landing page.

If you forget your password or want to configure a different secondary authenticator, click Having trouble signing in? > Reset Password or Reset Second Factor, and a reset link is sent to your email ID. The reset link expires after 15 minutes. To learn more, see Resetting the Login Credentials or MFA.
If your account is configured with MFA, you can sign in using an email OTP:
Enter your login ID. If you want the service to remember your login ID the next time you log in, select the Remember Me checkbox.
Click Next, and then click Other Sign-in Options.
See image.
The Sign-in Options window appears.
In the Sign-in Options window, click Email OTP.
See image.
Enter the OTP sent to your email address and click Sign In. The OTP expires after 15 minutes. If the OTP expires or you don't receive an OTP, click Resend to receive another OTP after 60 seconds.
See image.
Enter your login ID. If you want the service to remember your login ID the next time you log in, select the Remember Me checkbox.
Select the Sign-in using Security Key or Biometric checkbox.
See image.
Click Next.
Based on your configuration, enter your security key or complete the biometric to access the Authentication Service landing page.

If you want to configure with a different security key or biometric, click Having trouble signing in? > Reset Security Key or Biometric, and a reset link is sent to your email ID. The reset link expires after 15 minutes. To learn more, see Resetting the Login Credentials or MFA.
Click the Deception tile to access the Deception Admin Portal.
If Authentication Service is enabled, no other sign-in methods are allowed.

Zscaler recommends that you use the Authentication Service Admin Portal to configure primary and secondary external identity providers (IdPs). Contact Zscaler Support to subscribe to Authentication Service. To learn more, see About External Identity Providers.
If your account is configured to use single sign-on (SSO) with an IdP:
On the Sign In page, click Zscaler Login.
See image.
You are redirected to your IdP's login page. Enter your credentials.
If the login is successful, you are redirected back to the Deception Admin Portal.
Accepting the End User Subscription Agreement (EUSA)
When you log in for the first time, the Deception Admin Portal displays an EUSA. Click Accept to accept the EUSA.
You cannot activate your license without accepting the EUSA. You can read the full EUSA at any time.
Navigating within the Deception Admin Portal
The Deception Admin Portal contains the following items in the left-side navigation:
Investigate
Orchestrate
Miragemaker
Deceive
Settings
Search
System Messages
Account Settings
Help

The Deception dashboard (the Investigate tab) is the landing page that displays all the logged forensics and attacker information in a graphical format. You can leverage this information to reduce the mean time to detect (MTTD) and improve security efficiency. The dashboard allows you to monitor and analyze the activities that adversaries conduct on your decoys to understand their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
On the Orchestrate page, you can perform the following actions:
Automate rules.
Integrate with the security information and event management (SIEM) solutions and other log aggregation repositories to forward events.
Contain threats.
Enrich alerts.
Create API tokens for additional platform integration.
To learn more, see About Orchestrate.

On the Miragemaker page, you can configure built-in decoys and customize them to match your requirements. Miragemaker makes realistic-looking decoys scalable and provides built-in decoy datasets for a variety of use cases to launch deception campaigns rapidly. You can add or edit datasets for the decoys to serve as application content. This includes uploaded or dynamically generated files, web application interfaces, interactive web applications, interactive SCADA and IoT templates, custom text or binary protocols, etc. You can also load high-interaction containers.
To learn more, see Understanding the Miragemaker Module.

On the Deceive page, you can add, configure, and manage decoys to detect threats. You can deploy decoys across the public-facing perimeter, endpoints, network, cloud, and Active Directory (AD) to detect threats. You can also launch your first deception campaign with ready-to-use decoys and focus on detecting threats instead of configuring a new solution.
To learn more, see About Deceive.

On the Settings page, you can configure the prerequisites required for Deception, such as configuring a Decoy Connector, virtual local area networks (VLANs), or subnets. In addition, you can configure users and roles and view information regarding license consumption and audit trails.
To learn more, see About Settings.
Click the System Messages icon to view audit logs, system messages, and debug logs.
Click the Account Settings icon to reset your two-factor authentication (2FA), edit your profile, change your time zone, and change your password.
To learn more, see About Account Settings.
Click the Help icon to submit a ticket to Zscaler Support.
You can search for features, configurations, or events by entering keywords, with the drop-down menu offering organized paths to key sections.
